parts.text: Construction on the Big Bend border wall stayed paused as the contractor waited on a federal review.

wrapped._comment: The wrapper `validateSummary` strips rather than refuses — a chat-tuned model returns this often enough that refusing would make refusal the common case.

parts.text: **Summary:** "Construction on the Big Bend border wall stayed paused as the contractor waited on a federal review."

two_sentences._comment: Refused: the contract is one sentence, and two is the failure the cap cannot catch.

parts.text: The wall pause held through the morning. Officials would not say when work resumes.

abbreviated._comment: ACCEPTED, and the reason this fixture exists: 'U.S.' is a period, a space and a capital letter inside ONE sentence. A naive boundary test reads it as two and rejects every summary that names a country.

parts.text: U.S. Customs and Border Protection said Mr. Alvarez had signed the pause order that morning.

essay._comment: Refused on length. Not hypothetical — a model asked for prose pads a slow quarter rather than saying little.

parts.text: In a development that observers of the long-running border infrastructure dispute will recognise as characteristic of the wider pattern of federal-state friction that has defined the last several months of litigation, negotiation and quiet administrative delay, construction along the Big Bend stretch remained suspended.

thinking._comment: The shape gemma-4-26b-a4b-it returned on 2026-08-28: a `thought` part, then the answer. `answerText` must read the discriminator rather than concatenating.

parts.text: The coverage is about a construction pause; I should name the place and what happened.

truncated._comment: The whole output budget spent before a word was written — costs a summary, and is the one failure that IS a reason to raise maxOutputTokens.
